cards.text: Famine in the land. Another one, after the one back in Abraham's day. So Isaac, Abraham's son, goes to Abimelech, king of the Philistines, at Gerar.
Then the LORD appears to Isaac, and He's giving directions. Better than any map app, friend, because this one never says “recalculating.”

cards.question: The LORD tells Isaac not to go down to ___. He's to settle where God tells him.
God tells Isaac to stay in the land as a foreigner, and promises to give all these ___ to him and his offspring.

cards.text: God says He'll confirm the oath He swore to Abraham: descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky. Friend, I light ONE star per cookie box and I'm out here sweating.

cards.question: God tells Isaac that through his offspring, all nations of the earth will be blessed.
God says this promise comes because of something Abraham did. What was it?

cards.text: So Isaac settles in Gerar. Then the men there start asking about his wife, Rebekah.

cards.question: What does Isaac tell the men of Gerar about Rebekah?
Why does Isaac tell the men of Gerar that Rebekah is his sister?

answers.text: He's afraid they'll kill him for her
He hopes the king will give him land
He wants her to find a husband there

cards.text: Isaac's been in Gerar a long time. Then Abimelech looks down from the window, and friend, rule number one: never run a cover story under a king's window.

cards.question: What surprises Abimelech when he looks down from the window?

cards.text: Abimelech sends for Isaac: “So she is really your wife! How could you say, ‘She is my sister’?” Isaac tells him he thought he might die on account of her.

cards.question: Abimelech says one of his people could easily have slept with Rebekah, and Isaac would have brought ___ upon them.
Abimelech warns his people that whoever harms Isaac or Rebekah will surely be put to death.
Isaac sows seed in the land, and that very year he reaps a ___.

cards.text: The LORD blesses Isaac, and he gets richer and richer: flocks, herds, servants, the works. Me? I came out of a clearance bin for 25 cents, and I'm STILL proud of it.

cards.question: The Philistines are thrilled to see Isaac doing so well.
What do the Philistines do to the wells Abraham's servants had dug?
Then Abimelech tells Isaac to depart. What reason does Abimelech give?

answers.text: Isaac is too powerful for them

cards.text: So Isaac leaves and settles in the Valley of Gerar. There he reopens his father Abraham's wells, the ones the Philistines stopped up after Abraham died.

cards.question: Isaac gives his father's reopened wells brand new names of his own.

cards.text: Then Isaac's servants dig in the valley and find a well of fresh water. FRESH water, friend! I bet they were dancing around that hole like they won a prize.

cards.question: The herdsmen of Gerar show up and quarrel with Isaac's herdsmen, saying the water is ___.

cards.text: So Isaac names the well Esek, because they contended with him. He named a well after the FIGHT, like saving somebody in your phone as “Do Not Answer.”

cards.question: Isaac's servants dig a second well, and this time nobody quarrels over it.

cards.text: Second well, second quarrel, so he names that one Sitnah. Isaac moves on from there and digs another one.

cards.question: What happens at this next well Isaac digs?
Isaac names this well Rehoboth. What does he say the LORD has done?

cards.text: From there Isaac goes up to Beersheba. That night the LORD appears to him: “I am the God of your father Abraham.”

cards.question: The LORD tells Isaac He is with him. What does He tell Isaac not to do?
At Beersheba, Isaac builds an ___ and calls on the name of the LORD.

cards.text: Later, Abimelech comes from Gerar with Ahuzzath, his adviser, and Phicol, the commander of his army. When the king brings his adviser AND his army commander, you don't know whether to warm up the oven or hide behind it.

cards.question: Isaac asks Abimelech and his men why they've come. What does Isaac say they did to him?

answers.text: Hated him and sent him away
Mocked his God and his altar

cards.question: Abimelech's group says they can plainly see the LORD has been with Isaac. What do they want from him?

answers.text: An oath that he won't harm them
Half of his flocks and herds
His servants to fight their wars

cards.text: So Isaac prepares a feast, they eat and drink, and early the next morning they swear an oath to each other. The same crew that told him to leave, and they walk away fed and in PEACE.

cards.question: That same day, Isaac's servants come and tell him they've found water at the well they dug.

cards.text: Isaac calls the well Shibah, and to this day the city is called Beersheba. Then Esau, Isaac's son, turns forty and marries two Hittite women, Judith and Basemath.

cards.question: What do Esau's two wives bring to Isaac and Rebekah?

cards.text: Peace with the neighbors, grief at home. That's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this family's story is far from done.

findings.problem: The question tells the baker to 'stay in the land as a foreigner' and then blanks 'all these ___'. Having 'land' in the same sentence makes 'lands' stand out from 'herds' and 'treasures'.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke 'never run a cover story under a king's window' tells the baker the cover story is about to be exposed. That rules out 'Isaac counting his sheep' and 'Rebekah weaving with servants' before card 12 asks what Abimelech sees.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: No card sets up Isaac's harvest or blessing before this question. Telling 'hundredfold' apart from 'tenfold' or 'double' is pure luck, and the blank tests a detail of wording the baker hasn't seen rather than meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't share the fact's core action. Isaac is growing exceedingly wealthy, while Papa Dorin was bought for 25 cents and is 'STILL proud of it'. The contrast doesn't click instantly, and a stranger would likely say 'huh?'

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'There he reopens his father Abraham's wells' places the reopened wells in the Valley of Gerar. Genesis 26:18 doesn't say where those wells were.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The blank follows 'an' ('builds an ___'). Only 'altar' fits the article, so 'tower' and 'storehouse' are ruled out by grammar.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: Genesis 26:25 says Isaac's servants dug a well at Beersheba, but no card tells this (card 12 covers only the altar). Card 17 then refers to 'the well they dug' with no setup, so the baker misses the detail that ties the passage's ending together.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: 'Peace with the neighbors, grief at home' recaps the oath and verse 35, which card 19 just asked about, instead of moving the passage forward. The last verse is asked on a choice card, so this card can be just the line saying the story isn't over.
